plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks carry huge golden-rimmed flower heads with dark, seed-packed centers. Whole fields turn together toward the sun, which makes late-summer farmland look like a sea of yellow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midsummer to early autumn (roughly July to September)
plants.location: Northern Hemisphere, including the Great Plains of the United States and the farmlands of France and Ukraine
plants.funFact: What looks like one big flower is a composite head made of hundreds of tiny florets. Each floret can develop into a single seed.

plants.name: Calluna vulgaris
plants.description: Low, wiry shrubs cover open moorland in a haze of pink and purple. The tiny bell-shaped blooms hum with bees in late summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (roughly August to October)
plants.location: Moorlands and heaths of Scotland, northern England and northern Europe
plants.funFact: Heather honey is prized for its thick, jelly-like texture. Beekeepers sometimes move hives onto the moors in August to catch the bloom.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: This Australian tree is covered in fluffy, fragrant golden pom-poms that light up the bush at the end of winter. Its sickle-shaped leaves are blue-green and leathery.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (roughly July to October)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem. National Wattle Day is held on September 1, the day after this feature's date.
